_README: Response HEADER sets captured live from api.github.com on 2026-08-14, all
UNAUTHENTICATED (no PAT existed on this machine and none was requested).
Header names are lowercased as `fetch` normalizes them; values are verbatim
except where a `_redacted` note says otherwise.
These exist so tests/fetch/github.test.ts can serve REAL GitHub header shapes
from a real local http server, per the project's no-mocks rule. Inventing
these by hand is exactly what would have hidden the two findings below.
TWO FINDINGS THESE FIXTURES PIN, both contradicting the M4a plan's assumptions:
1. `search_repositories_200` carries NO etag and NO last-modified, and says
`cache-control: no-cache`. The Search API does not support conditional
requests at all. `repo_200` (Core API) does carry both. So the plan's
'wire ETag through' applies to Core only -- there is nothing to wire on
the endpoint the repos lane's search actually calls.
2. `repo_304` was produced by replaying `repo_200`'s etag as If-None-Match.
x-ratelimit-used went 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 across four such replays, i.e. a 304
DID consume budget. GitHub documents 304s as exempt; that exemption was NOT
observed on the unauthenticated path, which is the path that has the 60/hour
ceiling. Whether it holds WITH a PAT is unverified here -- no PAT exists.
3. `graphql_403` is a real primary-rate-limit-exceeded response, captured on the
first and only unauthenticated GraphQL request ever made from this machine.
`x-ratelimit-limit: 0` is not exhaustion -- the GraphQL budget is ZERO
unauthenticated. This is why src/fetch/github.ts is REST-only. Note it
carries NO retry-after: primary limits signal via remaining/reset, and
retry-after is the SECONDARY-limit signal. The client must read both.

repo_304._note: Body is empty by definition. `used` incremented -- see finding 2 above.

search_repositories_200._note: No etag. No last-modified. Deliberately recorded as absent, not omitted for brevity.

graphql_403._redacted: The real body named this machine's public IPv4 address. Replaced with 192.0.2.1 (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1) because this repository is PUBLIC. Nothing else in the body was altered.

_body.message: API rate limit exceeded for 192.0.2.1. (But here's the good news: Authenticated requests get a higher rate limit. Check out the documentation for more details.)

_note: NOT captured live. Deliberately so: producing one means abusing the API to
trip a secondary limit, which this project's politeness rule forbids and
which the M4a plan explicitly rules out ('respect rate-limit headers rather
than discovering limits by hitting them'). Header names and the retry-after
semantics are taken from GitHub's published documentation, and the client
must handle them because the real API will send them. Flagged here so no
future reader mistakes this one entry for observed evidence.
